title: Google Ads clicks land on the homepage
evidence: The ad click URL /?gad_source=1&gclid=… opens the homepage, and the ad-parameter URL is indexed by Google.
heuristic: Match between system and real world
fix: Intent-matched landing pages per campaign (gaming PCs, MacBook, monitors) and canonical tags that strip ad parameters.

title: Test and demo pages are public
evidence: /en/home-page-02-66d465ea485bb ('Golden EN Home Page Demo') and /en/category-test.html ('Category Test') are live and indexed.
fix: Unpublish or noindex; add a pre-release QA checklist.

title: Category shortcuts move between visits
evidence: Three loads of /ar/ showed the eight category tiles in three different orders (Servers, Scanners or Gaming PCs first). The row is a slider, so a returning shopper can't rely on position.
fix: A fixed grid of all top departments in a stable order, laptops and gaming first.

title: Typos in banners, footer and labels
evidence: Homepage banner 'PC GAMING Beyond pergormance.'; footer 'Usefull links', 'Warrnty & Maintenance', 'Informations', '© 2025'; product page 'SAR 1174.75or up to 12 months'; tiles labelled 'Intel Core i5' over Core Ultra artwork.
fix: Proofread banners, footer and widget copy in both languages before release.

title: Several offer pages compete
evidence: Eight offer pages are indexed; /offers.html and /laptops-computers-and-gaming-monitors-offers.html share a title; /mega-sale.html is titled 'Special Offers' and holds 'Back To School'.
fix: One 'Golden Offers' hub with campaign tabs and filters; redirect the rest.

title: Broken English in page titles and meta copy
evidence: 'Shop best Gaming laptop with in KSA'; 'Now can get your Laptop…'; 'Shop Now Laptop Gaming, PC Gaming & Monitors Gaming'; 'had established'.
heuristic: Match between system and real world
fix: Rewrite title and meta templates in native English and Arabic.

title: English and Arabic versions bleed into each other
evidence: Arabic titles are indexed on /en/ URLs; Arabic blog posts sit under /en/blog/; page titles read 'FAQ EN' and 'FAQs AR'; the Arabic homepage carries English-only banners.
fix: Fix hreflang and canonicals per store view; Arabic glossary; customer-facing page titles.

title: Navigation is by brand and product type, not by need
evidence: The departments menu lists 15 items, mixing brands (Apple, Microsoft, Promate) with types. There are no paths for study, creators or price bands.
fix: Card sort and tree test with Saudi shoppers; add 'Shop by need' (Study, Gaming, Work, Create) and price bands.

title: Some labels don't match their contents
evidence: 'Gaming' is titled for computers and laptops but lists peripherals; Servers holds one product; duplicate paths (/ar/laptop/microsoft and /ar/microsoft/laptop); breadcrumb 'Home » PC Gaming » PC Gaming'.
fix: Rename and merge categories; one canonical path each; fix the breadcrumb.

title: No business or quote path
evidence: The About page mentions a wholesale division, but there is no quote page. A shopper typed 'Please For Pc , Qty 2: DELL PC PRO QVT1260 …' into the search box. Checkout offers only an 'Is company?' tick box.
fix: 'Business' hub: request a quote, bulk pricing, VAT invoice, bank transfer or PO.

title: Recent searches appear to show other shoppers' queries
evidence: The 'recent searches' panel listed 'Please For Pc , Qty 2: DELL PC PRO QVT1260 I7-1400 16 GB /512 (KEY MOUSE With LED DELL One', which the auditor didn't type.
fix: Show only the shopper's own history (stored in their browser) plus curated popular searches.

title: Search result pages are indexed by Google
evidence: /en/catalogsearch/result/?amnoroute=&q=… and /?gad_source=1 appear in Google; a retired product URL lands on search results.
fix: Noindex search results; 301 retired products to their successor; canonical tags.

title: Product titles are long spec strings
evidence: Cards repeat a 115–140 character title ('PC Gaming Intel Core i5-14400F Processor, 16GB Ram, 1TB SSD M.2, RTX 3050 6GB GPU…'), truncated to two lines, above four spec lines that say the same thing.
fix: Title schema 'Brand Model' plus the spec lines; keep the long name for the product page.

title: Gaming PCs share one rendered image
evidence: Most builds on /en/pc-gaming.html use the same case render with a different GPU label. The product page shows one rendered spec card, with no photos or gallery visible.
fix: Photograph each build (front, side, inside, ports) and add a gallery; keep the spec card as one slide.

title: No build-your-own PC
evidence: A finder (Processor, Memory, Storage, Graphic card) narrows pre-builts, but shoppers can't configure a build. Newegg KSA, FEEH and GCC Gamers offer builders; eXtra, Jarir, Amazon.sa and noon don't.
fix: Guided PC builder with compatibility checks, FPS estimates and instalment price.

title: Delivery promise contradicts the Terms
evidence: Product page and checkout: 'Delivery in Riyadh: 24 hours, other cities: 3-6 business days.' Terms: Riyadh '3 to 7 working days', elsewhere '7 to 10'. FAQ: '3 to 7 days'.
fix: One promise per city, shown as a date ('Arrives Thu 24 Oct') with an order-by cut-off, from one setting used by every page.

title: No delivery date, delivery cost or accessory suggestions on the product page
evidence: The buy box shows a range of days and no delivery cost. No compatible accessories, protection plan or bundles were visible.
fix: Delivery block with date and cost; 'Complete your setup' bundle; optional extended warranty.

title: No customer reviews
evidence: The review section reads 'There are no ratings.' with an empty histogram; listings show 0–2 reviews per product.
fix: Post-delivery review requests over WhatsApp or SMS; show the store's Google rating site-wide.

title: Buy box is crowded and has two competing buttons
evidence: Before the specs: warranty bar, Free Gift banner, 5% MADA card banner, an instalments box, a Tamara box and a Tabby box with identical text, then gold 'Add to Cart' beside a heavier navy 'Buy Now', plus Wish List, Compare and Share.
fix: One instalment line with a details sheet; one primary button; promos below the buy box.

title: Free gift isn't explained
evidence: A 'Free Gift' banner shows a keyboard, mouse and headset with no names, value or terms.
fix: Name the items, their value and how the gift is added to the order.

title: Spec errors in titles and URLs
evidence: Samsung G90XF title says 4K, description says FHD 1920x1080. A 15IRX10 product sits at a 15IRX9 URL. An Arabic title breaks 'i7-13645HX' into '13645HX-7'.
fix: Spec attributes validated against the brand feed; titles generated from attributes.

title: Outdated models and duplicate product pages
evidence: M3 MacBook Air and Surface Pro 8 (Windows 10) are indexed; ASUS ROG Strix G614PR has two product URLs.
fix: Retire or redirect old SKUs; merge duplicates.

title: Prices differ between search-engine copies
evidence: Search copies show the Lenovo LOQ 15IRX10 at 6,899 SAR in English and 5,299 SAR in Arabic, and a Legion 5 at 16,449 on a listing vs 6,299 on its page. Live, the RTX 3050 build showed 4,699 SAR on listing, product page and cart, so some gaps may be timing.
fix: Daily automated price-parity check across store views and listings.

title: Policy pages give three different delivery fees
evidence: Terms: '20 SAR per order' and +20 SAR for cash on delivery. FAQ: 10 SAR under 200 SAR, free above. The live cart showed 0 SAR and 'Congratulations! You've earned free shipping!' on a 4,699 SAR order.
fix: Publish the real rule once (free above X SAR) and show it on product pages and in the cart.

title: Returns: 7 days, defects only
evidence: 'within (7) days', defects or wrong items only; excludes 'all computer accessories'; 'no return is made on any request in installments'; 59 or 79 SAR fees. The E-Commerce Law gives a 7-day cancellation right for unused items: legal review advised.
fix: 14-day change-of-mind returns for sealed items, plain exceptions, one fee, an online returns form; legal check.

title: Refund time stated as 1–5 days and as 3–30 days
evidence: Payment page: '1 to 5 business days'. Terms: 'from 3 days to 30 days'.
fix: One refund timeline per payment method in a single table.

title: Instalment offers are inconsistent and the payment page omits them
evidence: Homepage and product page: 'pay in 3 months with no fees, or up to 24 months', Tamara and Tabby '4 payments … or up to 12 months', '5% extra with code MADA'. Checkout labels Tabby and Tamara identically ('Pay 4 interest-free payments'). The Payment Methods page lists only Visa, Mastercard, mada and card instalments.
fix: One instalment message everywhere; name each provider at checkout; list every method on the payment page.

title: Warranty page disclaims responsibility for brand warranties
evidence: Store-built PCs carry '24 Months Warranty by Golden Tech'. For other products: '…provided by the agent are not considered the responsibility of The Golden Technology. The customer must contact directly with the agent.' 79 SAR courier fee for remote areas.
heuristic: Help users recognize, diagnose, and recover from errors
fix: A store-run warranty desk: Golden Tech opens and tracks the claim with the brand for the customer.

title: Legal and warranty pages read as raw machine translation
evidence: 'All electronic devices from Technology gold have been guaranteed…'; 'Accessories and accessories maybe have guaranteed…'; the company is named four different ways.
heuristic: Match between system and real world
fix: Professional bilingual rewrite of all policy pages, Arabic as source, with plain summaries on top.

title: Trust details are inconsistent
evidence: The footer shows CR, VAT number, a VAT badge and the Saudi Business Center logo. But the Terms say 'Golden Technology foundation', About says 'Trading Company', and 'authorized distributors' names no brand.
fix: One legal entity name; link the SBC logo to the store's certificate; named brand-authorisation badges.

title: Cart summary doesn't add up at a glance
evidence: Item shows 4699.00 SAR; Summary shows Subtotal 4,086 (before VAT), Tax 613, 'Total Savings -1,900' in green, Order Total 4,699. The savings line looks like a deduction the total doesn't reflect.
fix: Show the VAT-inclusive subtotal, move 'You save 1,900 SAR' out of the sum, and format prices the same way everywhere.

title: Checkout stalls on an unclear SMS-code step
evidence: After the mobile number is typed, red text says 'Please verify your phone number first.' The dark 'Send Otp' button looks disabled; the auditor couldn't tell whether it was active. The order can't be placed until the code is entered.
fix: Explain the step ('We'll text you a 4-digit code'), use an obvious active button, verify at Place Order, autofill the code.

title: FAQ says you must register; checkout says you don't
evidence: FAQ: 'You have to be a registered user to be able to make purchases'. Checkout: 'You can create an account after checkout.'
fix: Update the FAQ and say 'No account needed' on the cart and sign-in pages.

title: No National Address short-code field
evidence: Checkout has a map picker, City, District, Street, Building No and Postal code, but no Short Address field (4 letters + 4 digits). Carriers must reject parcels without a valid National Address since 1 Jan 2026.
fix: Add a Short Address field with format check and lookup that fills the other fields.

title: Cash on delivery and Apple Pay are advertised but not offered
evidence: The footer shows 'Aramex Cash on Delivery' and banners show Apple Pay. Checkout listed only cards/mada, Tabby, Tamara and card instalments (tested in Chrome; Apple Pay may appear only in Safari).
fix: Offer what's advertised or remove the logos; test Apple Pay in Safari on iPhone and Mac.

title: No WhatsApp or live chat; contact details differ
evidence: No WhatsApp or chat button on any page tested. Landline hours are 9:30am–10pm on one page and 8am–5pm on another; two emails (info@, online@).
fix: WhatsApp Business with catalogue and order updates; one contact page with hours per channel.

title: Cancellation and returns are phone-only
evidence: The footer has an 'Orders' link for account holders. Cancellation is by phone, with a 59 SAR fee after dispatch; returns start by phone or email.
fix: Guest order lookup, SMS or WhatsApp status updates, and a cancel button until dispatch.

title: Loyalty programme is thin
evidence: 1,000 points = 10 SAR; the validity period isn't stated; the programme can end 'without prior notice'.
fix: Tie points to accessories, setup and warranty perks; state the expiry.

title: Primary buttons come in five styles
evidence: Gold full-width on homepage cards and 'Checkout'; black on category cards, 'Sign In' and cart buttons; navy 'Buy Now'; dark slate 'Send Otp'; bright blue 'Place Order', a colour used nowhere else.
fix: One primary button token (fill, text, radius, height, states) applied everywhere, with one secondary style.

title: Gold is used for everything
evidence: Gold fills the departments button, active nav item, section tabs, search button, warranty bar, filter header, 'Write Review', newsletter button and Add to Cart. Gold link text on white ('Create an account') is faint.
fix: Reserve gold for the primary action; navy and neutrals for structure; dark text for gold-coloured links. Measure contrast.

title: Price block repeats itself and formats inconsistently
evidence: 'SAR 4,699 SAR 6,599 -29% Tax included Save SAR 1900' on the product page; '4699.00' in the cart; the discount chip sits far from the price.
fix: One price component: price, struck was-price, one saving chip, 'VAT included' caption, one number format.

title: Stock Magento wording and patterns
evidence: 'Update Shopping Cart' needed after changing quantity; 'Set Descending Direction'; 'find just the label you're looking for'; a Twitter bird icon after the rebrand to X.
heuristic: Match between system and real world
fix: Microcopy and component pass in both languages; auto-update the cart.
